A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MindJourney. All 23 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including appendices A-E, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAT evaluations, search and trajectory-description ablations, video-generation measurements, and qualitative failure analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original SAT evaluations and supplementary analyses, including a new runtime-accuracy experiment in Appendix C.3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.4 and A.2 replace CogVideoX-5B SWM with Wan2.2-TI2V-5B. Plucker/pitch conditioning through expanded input channels and LoRA tuning is replaced by learned extrinsic-matrix embeddings injected into transformer blocks, with only the camera encoder and projector fine-tuned. This substantially changes the world-model component; Spatial Beam Search remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain HM3D/Habitat, RealEstate10K, and DL3DV-10K training coverage; SAT-Real and SAT-Synthesized reasoning evaluation; and AI2-THOR video-generation evaluation. The added efficiency experiment introduces no stated new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, InternVL3-14B, o1, SVC, and the same cited SAT-Real reference baselines. The trajectory-description comparator sets are also unchanged. Wan and ReCamMaster enter as architectural sources, not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes the reported pruning-threshold sweep from {5,7,9} to {4,6,8}; Appendix A.2.3 changes the peak learning rate from 1e-4 to 3e-5. New Appendix C.3 measures runtime and accuracy across one to three search steps and 20 versus 50 generation iterations. Main evaluation splits, sample counts, and accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The search-depth/threshold sensitivity analysis is revised, and Appendix C.3 adds a focused study of generation iterations, search depth, runtime components, and accuracy. Existing trajectory-description ablations, world-model comparisons, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same plus/minus uncertainty entries. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, or significance tests for the reasoning evaluations, and v2 adds no uncertainty reporting to its timing study.

E6.justification: Central results are revised: Table 1 changes GPT-4.1 baseline/SWM averages from 67.3/82.6 to 74.0/80.6 and GPT-4o+SWM from 68.0 to 70.6. Table 2 changes InternVL3+SWM from 71.6 to 66.6. Figure 4 replaces the sensitivity curves, and new Table 4 adds six runtime-accuracy configurations. SWM changes preclude interpreting these as same-model gains or losses; v2's appendix trajectory tables retain the earlier scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2.2 removes the explicit Plucker-ray definition, pitch-rotation matrix, and horizontal-motion factorization used to construct the previous seven-channel action representation. The main trajectory-space and beam-search mathematics remain unchanged; neither version contains theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the headline average improvement from over 8% to 7.7%, while the introduction changes the largest gain from approximately 15% to over 10%. The central claims of training-free VLM enhancement, model independence, and compatibility with RL-based reasoning remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 qualifies depth-related trends by threshold and replaces the overly-strict-threshold explanation with greater sensitivity on real images due to lower generation quality. Appendix C.3 newly recommends two search steps and 20 generation iterations as a practical efficiency compromise. Existing limitations and failure explanations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 substantially replaces the implementation recipe: PatchEmbed initialization and rank/scale-128 LoRA details give way to camera-encoder injection locations and encoder/projector-only tuning. The explicit v-prediction objective, DDIM sampler, and nine-frame latency statement disappear. The CogVideo URL/license footnote is replaced by a ReCamMaster codebase referral, and C.3 adds component-level timing information.

R1.justification: SWM's stated architectural lineage changes from CameraCtrl/Memory-WM to ReCamMaster. References add Wan and ReCamMaster and remove CogVideoX, Sitzmann et al., Salimans and Ho, and Rombach et al. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the SWM implementation description and ablation discussion, with a new efficiency subsection and acknowledgments. The publication footer changes to NeurIPS 2025. The main narrative and section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn with revised threshold legends, percentage-scale axes, and an expanded caption. A runtime table is added; the existing trajectory-description tables become Tables 5-6 and move later in the appendix, while prompt figures are redistributed. Other diagrams and qualitative examples retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new efficiency study provides useful practical evidence: two search steps with 20 iterations yield 68.6% accuracy in 26.93 seconds versus 70.6% in 161.48 seconds for three steps with 50 iterations. However, v2 changes SWM and main results while retaining unexplained conflicting appendix scores: GPT-4.1 baseline/SWM is 74.0/80.6 in Table 1 but 67.3/82.6 in Table 5. It also omits the previous explicit objective and sampler specification. These unresolved consistency and reproducibility issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
